symbols.name: first bit
symbols.meaning: A bit, one of the two inputs to the exclusive or.
symbols.quote: For bits $\delta$ and $\epsilon$, the exclusive or $\delta \oplus \epsilon$ is their bitwise sum modulo 2, which is 1 exactly when the bits differ.

symbols.name: second bit
symbols.meaning: A bit, the other input to the exclusive or.
symbols.quote: For bits $\delta$ and $\epsilon$, the exclusive or $\delta \oplus \epsilon$ is their bitwise sum modulo 2, which is 1 exactly when the bits differ.

symbols.name: XOR operation
symbols.meaning: The exclusive-or operation, the bitwise sum modulo 2 of two bits, applied at each position to bit strings of equal length.
symbols.quote: For bits $\delta$ and $\epsilon$, the exclusive or $\delta \oplus \epsilon$ is their bitwise sum modulo 2, which is 1 exactly when the bits differ.

relations.quote: XOR is a step inside the [address-field interchange procedure](address-interchange.md), which swaps two fields of address bits.
Hence a sequence of such steps can produce a [permutation](permutation.md) of the data, which is a rearrangement of positions with each position used once.
Pointwise XOR is the only gate of the [bit network](bit-network.md) in the paper
XOR is the operation of a [gate applied pointwise](network-gate-terminal.md), which acts at each address separately on the bits stored there.
